habitat: Singly or in pairs in thornveld, woodland, coastal bush and plantations, in the lower stratum.
summary: A common resident. Told by the black crown, with a beige mantle and rufous wings. The immature has a blackish-brown crown and a horn-coloured bill. The alarm is krok-krok-krokrakror. The song is a loud, ponderous, flat whistled series, cheer-tcharee, trichi cheer-tcharoo, cheeroo, cheeroo. Pairs also duet with grating, churring and whistling calls. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Brown-crowned Tchagra is smaller, with a grey-brown crown separated from the eyebrow by a black line, and it is more buff-brown.
